items.title: Japanese court says voice is protected by publicity rights; US appeals court says AI training is not fair use
items.summary: There have been two judgments this week of relevance to the ongoing AI debates in the music industry. A Japanese court ruled that publicity rights allow performers to stop unapproved AI voice clones. Meanwhile a US appeals court ruled against an AI company that used the good old fair use defence

items.title: US appeals court rejects ‘fair use’ defense over AI training – as Thomson Reuters wins copyright case backed by RIAA and NMPA
AI Lost Its First Fair Use Appeal. Suno Should Be Worried.
Suno AI y GEMA: la batalla por los derechos de autor que puede redefinir el negocio de la música para la IA
Historic ruling on 'fair use' and AI may help Nashville songwriters
Trump’s DoJ was biased and wrong about ‘fair use’, say news orgs in OpenAI dispute
items.summary: Many of the music industry’s AI legal battles swing on whether or not AI training is ‘fair use’ under US copyright law. Donald Trump’s DoJ recently intervened in a dispute between newspapers and OpenAI insisting AI training is fair use. The newspapers have responded, explaining why the DoJ is wrong

items.title: Suno is ‘far beyond’ 2m subscribers and $300m in revenue, says Mikey Shulman – who argues it’s ‘good’ that AI music has no ‘firm rules of the road’ yet
items.summary: Shulman also set out what WMG and BMG get from their deals, and who should be setting AI's rules. Source

items.title: Kelly Clarkson Says ‘I Love AI’ but AI Artists Should Not Be on the Same Music Charts as Humans
items.summary: Kelly Clarkson has shared her admittedly “controversial” opinion on artificial intelligence, saying she thinks it can do “amazing things” but shouldn’t be able to create anything that competes with humans, particularly on music charts. The pop star shared her feelings about the technology during an appearance on the La…

items.title: IMPF and IMPEL publish AI licensing principles, insisting songs and recordings must be valued equally
items.summary: As the music industry enters into ever more deals with AI platforms, the indie publisher community has again insisted that - with AI - song rights and recording rights must be valued equally, unlike in streaming. A new AI framework from IMPF and IMPEL says that key principle is “non-negotiable”

tip.title: Los covers necesitan licencia aunque des crédito
tip.body: Acreditar al autor no sustituye la licencia. Para publicar un cover en plataformas necesitas la licencia mecánica correspondiente, y para usarlo en video, además, la sincronización.

tip.title: Covers need a license even if you give credit
tip.body: Crediting the songwriter is not a license. Releasing a cover on platforms requires a mechanical license, and using it in a video also requires a sync license.
